verses.1: And when they went to Jerusalem and arrived at Bethphage, near the Mount of Olive, then Jesus sent two of his disciples.
verses.2: He said to them, “Go into the village that’s opposite you. You will immediately find someone who is tied up, along with a cart attached to her. Unbind her and bring her to me.”
verses.3: And if anyone says anything to you, remember that their Lord has a need for them. Then, immediately dismiss them from your service.
verses.4: This happened in order to fulfill what the prophet had said.
verses.5: You said to the daughter of Sion, “Now, your king will bring you peace and prosperity, as well as a son from a concubine.”
verses.6: Then the disciples went out and did as Jesus had commanded them.
verses.7: They took the child and the lamb, and they placed their clothes on them. Then they stood above them.
verses.8: The majority of the crowd threw their sleeves over their faces while walking along the road. Others cut off branches from the trees and threw them onto the road as well.
verses.9: But those who led him and those who followed him cried out, saying, “Praise be to the son of David! Praise be to him who comes in the name of the Lord!” They were among the most prominent people in that place.
verses.10: And when he entered Jerusalem, the entire city rushed out to meet him. They said, “Who is this man?”
verses.11: But the crowd said, “This is the prophet Jesus, who came from Nazareth in Galilee.”
verses.12: And Jesus entered the temple. He ordered all those who were selling and buying in the temple to stop their activities. He also destroyed the tables used by those who sold things there. He also destroyed the seats where people sat while they were selling.
verses.13: And he said to them: “It will be written that my house will be called a house of prayer. But you, instead, make it a den of thieves.”
verses.14: And those who were blind and deaf in the temple also came to him. He healed them.
verses.15: Seeing what wonders he had created, as well as the children who were shouting and singing in the temple, the high priests and the officials were filled with wonder. They said to David’s son, “These are truly wonders worthy of being shown to David.”
verses.16: And they said to him, “Do you hear what they are saying?” But Jesus replied to them, “Yes. Have you never heard that I am the one who speaks from the mouths of children and infants?”
verses.17: And after leaving them, he went out of the city into Bethany. There, he was healed.
verses.18: Then, he rushed back towards the city.
verses.19: And when he saw a vine along the road, he went up to it. But he found nothing in it except for its leaves. He said to it, “Do you still bear fruit during the summer?” Then the vine withered away.
verses.20: And seeing this, the disciples were amazed and said, “How can the vine grow when it has been cut off?”
verses.21: Then Jesus replied to them, “I tell you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you can do what is impossible. Not only will you be able to pick up snakes, but you can also say to this mountain, ‘Be taken up and thrown into the sea.’”
verses.22: And all those things you ask for in your prayers, may they be granted to you.
verses.23: And when he entered the temple, the high priests and the elders of the people came forward to teach him. They said, “In what authority do you do these things? And who gave you this authority?”
verses.24: Then Jesus replied to them, “I will ask you a question. If you tell me the answer, I will tell you in some form what I will do.”
verses.25: Where did John’s baptism come from? From heaven or from people? They argued among themselves, saying, “If we say it came from heaven, then we are wrong.” Why didn’t you believe him?
verses.26: But if we say that it’s a human being, then we should be afraid of the crowd. After all, everyone regards John as a prophet.
verses.27: And when they answered Jesus, they said, “We do not know.” He also said to them, “Neither do I tell you in any way that I do these things with any authority.”
verses.28: What do you think, then? He had two sons. When he went to see the first son, he said, “Son, go and work in the vineyard today.”
verses.29: But the one who replied said, “I don’t want to.” Later, after changing his mind, he left.
verses.30: When he came to the second time, he said the same thing. But the one who answered said, “I am it, Lord.” And he did not leave.
verses.31: Which of the two did he create as the offspring of the father? They say: The first one. Jesus said to them, “I tell you that both the male and female will bring you into the kingdom of God.”
verses.32: For John came to you in the way of justice, yet you did not believe him. But those who were evil and corrupt people believed him. You, however, did not pay any attention to him after you believed in him.
verses.33: You’ve heard another parable. There was a man who owned a vineyard. He built a fence around it and planted vines within it. Then he built a tower in it. People from other places came to work in his vineyard. But he drove them away.
verses.34: And when the time came for harvesting the fruits, he sent his servants to ask the farmers to bring back those fruits.
verses.35: And when the farmers took their slaves, they would either keep some of them, sell others, or use them as labor.
verses.36: Once again, more slaves were sent to them, in addition to those who had been sent before. They did the same things to them.
verses.37: Then he sent his son to them, saying, “Take my son away.”
verses.38: But when the farmers saw their son, they said to themselves, “This is his successor. Let us kill him and thus take away his inheritance.”
verses.39: And when they took him out of the vineyard, they burned him.
verses.40: So, when the master of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?
verses.41: They say to him, “He will destroy them in a cruel manner. The wine will be given to other farmers, since they will give him the fruits at the right time.”
verses.42: Jesus said to them, “You have never read the scriptures. The stone that the builders rejected became the head of the building. It was given by the Lord. Is it not wonderful to us?”
verses.43: Therefore, I say to you that the kingdom of God will be established without your participation, and it will be given to a people who will carry out God’s will.
verses.44: And whoever falls onto this stone will suffer greatly; no one else will be able to save him from that fate.
verses.45: And when the high priests and the Pharisees heard these parables, they understood that he was speaking about them.
verses.46: And when they tried to keep him, they were afraid of the crowd, because they considered him to be a prophet.
